run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-17T10:01:01Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is driven by error spans that fraud-detection records on its long-lived flagd subscription stream, not by failures in its order-processing path. Every ERROR-status span attributed to service_name=fraud-detection in the read window sits on span_name 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (10 distinct per-instance series, SPAN_KIND_CLIENT) or 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt' (2 series); its consumer spans 'orders receive'/'orders process' carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET. The 10 EventStream spans each lasted 594-602s, started 09:09:38Z-09:11:26Z and ended with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). In the same traces flagd's own server-side spans (service flagd v0.12.8, parented to the client stream spans) record rpc.grpc.status_code=4 with otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout', i.e. the shared flagd dependency terminated the streams. The same wave hit ad (7 such spans, 596.9-604.2s, code 4) and recommendation (3 spans, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), so the common factor is flagd rather than any single caller. flagd never restarted (pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx created 09:06:55Z, containers started 09:06:57Z, restartCount 0), all flags in ConfigMap flagd-config are 'off', no NetworkPolicy objects exist, and all 10 fraud-detection pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts. The alert's stated value 0.0222 equals 10/450, consistent in magnitude with 10 errored EventStream spans against the observed span volume, but the alerting rule itself was not returned by Prometheus and increase()-based 1h/23h error ratios computed for fraud-detection at 10:01:01Z evaluate to 0, so the exact evaluation formula could not be reproduced. Not verified: whether the ~600s stream termination recurs after ~09:31Z (span-metric series unreadable past ~09:31Z) and whether configuration changed around 09:20Z (change history not integrated).

claims.text: The only ERROR-status spans recorded for service_name=fraud-detection in the read window are on span_name 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (raw summed counter rising 1 -> 6 -> 10 between 09:21 and 09:23 then flat at 10) and 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt' (constant 2); its spans 'orders receive' and 'orders process' carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

The metric label sets show the fraud-detection EventStream ERROR spans are client spans (span_kind SPAN_KIND_CLIENT) exported from 10 distinct exported_instance series (5f790767-c742-4675-a312-a9d7cd3a7f9a, 743e11a8-2f4a-4d3e-b412-ffbc60f595e5, 8675d6e8-3e11-43e6-9bb6-c4ae8e948cb8, 8a54dd58-9464-42c9-97bb-0a8fe4503e03, 94a0681c-9e25-473b-b9a2-3b5eeb3a603a, 96250b84-64d4-451d-85c7-0be9a0d94789, 9a614662-7835-4453-99a5-5d5bd6a6ee48, 9a9a52cd-705b-40b0-916c-d72a3d2e6344, c06a3724-283f-42eb-9f08-e55031828a25, ee7fc181-5100-4bd6-a6e9-71afd782dba6), i.e. one failed stream span per fraud-detection instance.

Ten fraud-detection spans of operation 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (service_version 2.1.3) are all status_state recorded with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4, with durations 594101234-601796702 microseconds and start times 1794906578633500-1794906686430840 (09:09:38Z-09:11:26Z), so they terminated around 09:19:38Z-09:21:26Z; in the same result flagd server spans parented to fraud-detection stream spans carry otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout' and rpc.grpc.status_code=4.

Whole trace fbd86f0af8ba06b338f8aa19dcd4f1c9 contains ad's client span 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (600197748 us, error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4) and, as its visible child, flagd's server span (537999655 us, service_version v0.12.8) with the same code 4 and otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'.

The same stream-termination wave affected other flagd clients: ad shows 7 error spans on 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (596886931-604202243 us, rpc.grpc.status_code=4, starts 09:13:47Z-09:15:14Z) and recommendation shows 3 error spans on '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' of exactly 600005183-600006346 us with StatusCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED / grpc_status:4 raised in the gRPC client, plus flagd server spans carrying 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'.

flagd was not restarted or replaced during the wave: pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx was created 2026-11-17T09:06:55Z, its containers flagd and flagd-ui started 09:06:57Z with restartCount 0, init container init-config terminated Completed exit 0, and its owner is ReplicaSet flagd-58db7486bd.

All 10 fraud-detection pods (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-*) are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, no waiting reason and no last-termination reason; the flagd Deployment has 1 desired/1 ready replica and the fraud-detection Deployment 10 replicas.

Every fault-injection setting named in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'; all three flagd clients point at FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, and the flagd container has no args configured.
No NetworkPolicy objects exist in the cluster (the query over kind=networkpolicies processed 0 items), so a network policy cannot explain connections to flagd being dropped.

The alert value 0.0222222 equals 10/450, consistent with the 10 errored flagd EventStream client spans that are the only ERROR spans fraud-detection produced against the roughly 450-span volume visible in its span-metrics snapshots; the exact alerting expression could not be read, so this arithmetic match is an inference, not a confirmed formula.

The stream terminations look like a bounded ~600s server-side stream lifetime in flagd rather than one-off failures: all three client services' EventStream spans end at 594-604s regardless of client language (fraud-detection, ad, and recommendation in Python), and several durations exceed 600s (601.8s, 604.2s), which argues against a strict client deadline and for flagd closing the stream.

The alert's stated value cannot be reproduced with increase()-based ratios: at 2026-11-17T10:01:01Z the 1h ratio and the 23h ratio of ERROR spans to all spans both evaluate to 0 for fraud-detection, while frontend (0.000356), frontend-proxy (0.000352) and checkout (0.000731) are the only services with a nonzero ratio; separately, a 1h increase at 10:14:09Z reports 0 ERROR and 154 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans for fraud-detection.

The other error spans in the window belong to a different failure and are not fraud-detection's: trace c704e173b535ced0ec290ed149359b8e at 09:20:56Z shows checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' failing with 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post "http://shipping:8080/get-quote": EOF' (rpc.grpc.status_code 13, HTTP 500 propagated through frontend-proxy, frontend and load-generator).

fraud-detection pod restarts, crashes or evictions are not the cause: every fraud-detection pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, no last-termination reason and no waiting reason, and the window's events contain no Killing, Unhealthy, BackOff or Failed events for fraud-detection pods (the only otel-demo Pod events are Normal 'Killing' events for recommendation pods during its scale-down).

An injected fault flag is not the cause: no flag in flagd-config has an 'on'/non-zero defaultVariant, so no flag-declared fault (e.g. kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, adFailure) matches the observed flagd stream-termination failure path.

Inspect the flagd Deployment's gRPC EventStream lifetime/keepalive behaviour (and flagd v0.12.8 defaults) to confirm the ~600s stream re-establishment cycle, since no args, env var or ConfigMap entry exposing a stream timeout is present in the objects that can be read.

Retrieve the rule that emits RequestErrorRate to confirm its expression and evaluation window, and consider excluding flagd EventStream DEADLINE_EXCEEDED re-establishment spans from the service error-rate SLI (or not recording that re-establishment as an error span) if the ~600s cycle is expected behaviour.

gaps: Prometheus returned no alerting or recording rules at all (list_prometheus_rules returned nothing, status no_data, including for rule_name=RequestErrorRate), so the alert's expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown; the 0.0222 value was only matched arithmetically, not reproduced.

The trace span-metrics series for fraud-detection could not be read after about 09:31Z even though the query window ends 10:14:09Z (several range queries over 09:30-10:14 returned nothing, status no_data), so the error rate at the alert start 10:01:01Z and whether the flagd stream closures recurred after 09:31Z are unknown.

Application logs were empty for every pod tried (flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l, frontend-675fd7b5c5-c79h6; 0 lines, status no_data), so flagd-side and fraud-detection-side runtime messages about the stream timeouts could not be read.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so whether otel-demo/flagd-config, Deployment flagd or Deployment fraud-detection changed around 09:20Z - when the first EventStream span was created and terminated - cannot be verified.

Metrics queries for kube_pod_owner, kube_pod* and kube_deployment_status* returned nothing (status no_data), so pod ownership and workload status could only be read as current API state, not historically for the incident window.

No trace search matched fraud-detection error=true over 09:15-09:40Z (status no_data) and a search for operation 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' on service fraud-detection returned nothing (status no_data); fraud-detection stream errors are evidenced only by the error-status spans returned by min_duration and by the span-metrics series, so their per-span error detail text remains unread (the 'stream closed due to server-side timeout' description is observed on flagd server spans in the same traces).

The exact error detail on the fraud-detection EventStream client spans is not present in the sampled rows (only status tags), and the ad and recommendation client spans differ in detail (code 4 only vs. Python DEADLINE_EXCEEDED traceback).

kafka pods kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w (3 restarts, last termination reason Error, exit code 1) and kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr (1 restart, Error, exit 1) restarted at an unknown time during the window; their cause is unknown and no evidence ties them to the fraud-detection error rate.

HorizontalPodAutoscaler Warning events (FailedGetResourceMetric / FailedComputeMetricsReplicas against pods.metrics.k8s.io for kafka, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart, FailedGetScale for postgres, and recommendation scale-down 10->8->7) occurred at 09:20-09:23Z; they were not tied to the fraud-detection error rate and the metrics-server outage cause is unknown.
next_steps: Read the Prometheus rule that produces RequestErrorRate (expression, range, threshold) to confirm whether it counts flagd EventStream client spans and over what window.
Collect flagd logs and its gRPC server stream-lifetime configuration to confirm whether the ~600s stream termination is configured behaviour and whether clients are expected to reconnect silently.
Check the cluster's change history for ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, Deployment flagd and Deployment fraud-detection around 2026-11-17T09:15Z-09:25Z.

If the ~600s stream cycle is expected, adjust the error-rate SLI to exclude flagd EventStream re-establishment errors, or configure flagd flag providers so stream renewal does not produce DEADLINE_EXCEEDED error spans.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
